title: Account Escalation Lanes and Runway Hedging for Roadmap Capacity Allocation
creator: Aisha Bhandari
description:
Problem: We receive ad-hoc high-priority escalation requests from strategic accounts that can displace planned roadmap work, creating churn in delivery and missed OKR commitments. Current intake only captures account priority and a free-form ask, leaving product and eng teams to negotiate scope under time pressure.

Goal: Create a structured intake and allocation mechanism that converts strategic account signals into a bounded runway (time/effort) and a hedging policy so that escalations can be accepted, deferred, or fast-tracked with predictable impact to roadmap capacity and OKRs. This will reduce surprise scope changes, improve SLA conversations with sales/CS, and preserve sprint predictability while preserving a fast path for critical customer failures or contractual commitments.
proposal:
1) Define three escalation lanes (Operational Emergency, Strategic Commitment, Opportunity Acceleration) with explicit minimum acceptance criteria and a pre-agreed runway budget.
2) Allocate a rolling 'escalation runway' capacity per quarter (e.g., 6 engineer-weeks per 10 top accounts) that is book-kept against roadmap capacity.
3) Introduce a lightweight Triage Card template capturing impact, contractual obligation, reproducibility, rollback/fallback, and required SLA.
4) Decision flow: CS -> PM intake -> Triage committee (PM/Eng/SE/Success) -> Lane assignment -> Accept with runway / Request More Info / Defer to next quarter.
5) Update roadmap tooling to represent reserved runway capacity and produce automated 'what-if' holdback reports for OKR owners.
acceptance_criteria: Documented lane definitions and acceptance checklist published in Confluence
Triage Card template implemented in intake form and available to CS/AE
Roadmap UI can display 'reserved runway' allocation by team and decrement when tickets are accepted
Triage committee charter and membership finalized (PM, Eng lead, Solutions Eng, CS lead)
A pilot is run for Q2 with at least 5 strategic accounts to validate process and collect metrics
success_metrics: Reduction in unplanned sprint work from escalations by 50% vs. last quarter
Time from CS escalation to lane decision <= 72 hours for Operational Emergency and Strategic Commitment lanes
OKR delivery slippage caused by post-planning escalations reduced to <5% of committed scope
Satisfaction score from CS/sales about escalation handling >= 4/5 in pilot accounts
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize lane definitions, Triage Card template, and triage charter
Week 2: Integrate intake form into CS tooling and train CS/AE on use
Week 3-4: Small pilot (5 accounts), weekly triage committee sync and rapid iteration
End of quarter: Review pilot metrics, adjust runway sizing formula, and propose org-wide rollout for Q3
risks: Under- or over-sized runway allocation leading to wasted reserved capacity or insufficient buffer
CS adoption lag if intake adds perceived friction
Conflicts over what qualifies for Strategic Commitment lane without clear contract links
Tooling changes to roadmap UI take longer than expected (dependency on ENG-48234)
notes: Runway sizing heuristic: start with 6 engineer-weeks per 10 top accounts and adjust after pilot based on observed acceptance rate.
We should coordinate with Legal for any hard SLAs tied to Strategic Commitment lane
Consider a 'fast-fallback' automation: if triage committee misses SLA window, default lane = Operational Emergency for remediation tasks only

Schedule triage committee weekly recurring meeting (owner: Ethan Morales)
Build intake form prototype and QA with 2 CS reps
Add roadmap reserved-capacity field to product backlog schema (ENG ticket created)
